authorized_evidence.content:
Change Freeze

Northstar observes deployment freezes during payroll close, quarter-end financial reporting, and announced customer migration windows. The change calendar is the source of truth. Older release notes or team chat messages do not override the current freeze calendar.

Release Windows

Standard production deployments occur Tuesday through Thursday between 10:00 and 15:00 Eastern Time. Deployments outside that window require approval from the Engineering Manager on call and a written reason in the change record.

Friday deployments are limited to severity-one fixes, security patches approved by IT Admin, or customer-impacting incidents where waiting would increase risk. Weekend deployments require the incident commander to approve the change before execution.

Deployment Approval

| Change Type | Required Review | Required Approver |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Documentation-only release | Peer review | Team lead |
| Low-risk application change | Peer review and automated tests | Team lead |
| Database migration | Peer review, rollback plan, staging proof | Engineering Manager |
| Security-sensitive change | Peer review, IT Admin review | Engineering Manager |
| Emergency hotfix | Incident commander review | Engineering Manager on call |

All production changes must include a rollback plan. A rollback plan that says "revert if needed" is not sufficient; it must name the specific revert, migration rollback, feature flag, or mitigation.

Working Hours

Standard collaboration hours are 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time from Monday to Thursday. Teams may define additional overlap windows when customer coverage or release coordination requires it.

Employees should keep calendars accurate and mark focus time when unavailable. Repeated inability to meet team collaboration expectations should be discussed with the employee's manager.

Legal Hold

When Legal issues a hold notice, normal deletion schedules stop for the named matter. Recipients must preserve email, chat, files, ticket records, and notes that relate to the hold. Managers must confirm that affected team members understand the hold within five business days.

raw_response.answer: The usual release window for production deployments is Tuesday through Thursday between 10:00 and 15:00 Eastern Time, and deployments outside this window require approval from the Engineering Manager on call with a written reason in the change record. However, deployment freezes during announced customer migration windows are governed by the change calendar, which is the source of truth. Older release notes or team chat messages do not override the current freeze calendar. Therefore, the release window alone does not settle whether a Thursday release can proceed during a customer migration freeze; the change calendar controls the freeze. Additional deployment approvals and rollback plans are also required depending on the change type. What remains unsupported by the available documents is whether any specific override or exception process exists for releases during a migration freeze beyond the change calendar and usual approval processes.
